title: を (direct object)
meaning: Marks the direct object of a transitive verb; also the place passed through / left.
simpleExplanation: を marks the thing that an action is done to: パンを食べます "I eat bread" (bread receives the eating). It is written を but pronounced お. A second use: with verbs of movement it marks the place you move through or leave: 公園を散歩します "walk through the park", 家を出ます "leave the house".
whenUsed: With any action verb that does something to something: eat, drink, read, write, buy, watch, do. Also with 出る (leave), 歩く／散歩する (walk through), 渡る (cross), 降りる (get off).
formation: Noun + を + action verb  (本を読む)
Place + を + 出る／出発する  (家を出る)
Place + を + 歩く／散歩する／渡る  (道を渡る)

examples.note: Basic use: the thing eaten takes を.

examples.reading: こうえんを さんぽします。
examples.note: Movement through a space: "through the park".

examples.reading: しちじに いえを でます。
examples.en: I leave the house at seven.
examples.note: Leaving a place: 家を出ます.

examples.reading: まいばん テレビを みます。

examples.ja: 次の駅で電車を降ります。
examples.reading: つぎの えきで でんしゃを おります。
examples.en: I get off the train at the next station.
examples.note: Getting off (leaving) the train uses を; the place where it happens uses で.

similarGrammar.difference: Likes, abilities and wants (好き・できる・ほしい) take が, not を, because they are not actions.
で marks WHERE an action happens (公園で遊ぶ); を marks the space you move through (公園を歩く).
に marks the destination (家に帰る); を marks the place you leave (家を出る).

commonMistakes.why: 飲む is an action verb, so the thing drunk takes を.
好き is not an action; its object takes が.
Leaving a place uses を. に would mean going to the house.

usageNotes: Pronounced お. Verbs of movement (歩く・走る・散歩する・出る・降りる) take を for the space traversed or departed.
jlptTips: If the word after the blank is a verb like 食べます・飲みます・読みます・見ます・買います・します, the answer is を.
を also appears with 出ます・散歩します・歩きます・渡ります. Do not switch to で or に just because the noun is a place.
